questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: An exotic destination but at the same time high educational standards.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, everything is clear

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Needed assistances with finding one of my lecture buildings, anc everyone was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Depending on how picky you are, it is easy. It can be very expensive, and you probably have to stay a bit outside the CBD.
Use
flatmates.com.au
and the facebook page Fairyflossers, where there is plenty of rooms being posted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All the suburbs have their charm, there is no need to stay in the CBD.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit complicated to figure out where to find the different subjects but once you've found it, it is easy to figure out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you choose the subjects you want to enrol in, I had to prove i had the right pre-requisites and afterwards when they got accepted, I could choose what workshops and prac-labs I wanted to join, making my own itinerary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a Student service available everyday that is very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: totally succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you are unsure about what subject to enrol in, just choose one and try it out for the first week, you can always change it even after arrival.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses are generally high. The teachers are really enthutiastic and care about the studednts learning outcome and are helpful with further questions and explanations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from UCPH. There are a lot more assignments and I had 2-3 tests in all my classes during the semester while having normal lectures, and they all counted towards the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Stem Cell in Development and Regeneration
Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry
Microbes, Infection and Responses
Protein, Structure and Function

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend doing the Stem cells in Development and Regeneration, as many other courses are building on top of your already existing knowledge, but this is all new and really interesting with top researchers presenting their work in lectures. 
Also the Microbes, Infections and Responses is an interesting subject learning about microbes,  but also a lot about the immune system.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
the costs of the public transport was a lot higher than I expected. 
Just the everyday living is also high. You want to go to all the cafés and restaurants while you're here so that costs a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Beers are a lot more expensive than in DK. 
Many fruits and vegetables (like tomatoes and capsicum) are really expensive. 
Sushi is really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a ton of social clubs and sport activities to join at UniMelb. Almost whatever you can think of, there is.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Mounteneering club, they organise both one-day and multi-day hiking trip to really cool places.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definetly go camping at the Grampians. Also, dont forget to relax on your weekends to recharge for a new week even though you want to see and experience everything.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Australia is very much the same in many ways.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dont be afraid to talk to your new class mates, many of them dont know each other either and they are also looking for friends and for people to look over assignments with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the very laid back culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring more warm clothes than you think you are gonna need when arriving in Juli. It's COLD.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Campus is really big, download Lost on Campus app, it tells where everything from lecture halls to microwaves and libraries are.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When something traumativ happens and I realised how far away I was from home. Luckily, I met so many great people here, that cared for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
